# Summary of Harness Candidate Execution

The harness shows severe learning failures across all three datasets, with evaluation accuracies of 0% (ds_alpha), 23% (ds_beta), and uniformly poor performance (ds_gamma). A critical recurring pattern is that the model consistently predicts tokens extracted directly from the input sequence rather than generating the required structured outputs (hyphenated compound words), indicating the harness fails to guide the LLM toward the correct answer format. In ds_beta with multiple-choice options, the model collapses to repetitively predicting a single answer ("bragro-dorsto") regardless of context, suggesting severe mode-collapse rather than genuine learning. The memory mechanism remains completely unused (empty state throughout all steps), and in-context demonstration quality appears insufficient—the shallow reasoning "Closest demonstrations suggest X" appears mechanically for every prediction. Addressing the answer format specification in prompts, improving demonstration diversity, and leveraging the memory system for dynamic context building would be essential starting points for improvement.
